titleEn: Why Only a Little at a Time?

pages.text: All the snow in the forest had melted. Sap began to rise inside the birch trees. Grandpa Bruno put a little spout into a tree.
Drip. Drip. Clear sap fell into a bucket. It smelled a little sweet. Nils wanted to drink a whole cup of tree sap.
Nils looked inside the bucket. There was barely a drop at the bottom. "Why does it only come a little at a time?"
Nils took the bucket and shook it. Slosh, slosh. There still wasn't enough for even one sip.
This time Nils took the bucket down and tilted it. A drop fell out of the bucket.
While hanging the bucket back up, Nils lost hold of it. Rumble, tumble! The bucket fell and rolled away.
The sap that had collected slowly soaked into the ground. The bucket was empty again. Tears filled Nils's eyes.
Grandpa hung the bucket back up. "Tree sap comes one drop at a time. Drops never hurry."
Nils sat beside the bucket and watched the birds. A woodpecker tapped, and a little tit fluttered. From the bucket came drip, drip.
Shiny sap collected in the bucket. Nils poured a full cup and drank it. "Sweet! It tastes like waiting."
